title: Evens on Even Slots, Odds on Odd Slots
statement:
You get an array nums of even length in which exactly half of the values are even and half are odd.

Rearrange it so that every even index holds an even value and every odd index holds an odd value, and return the result. Any arrangement that follows the rule is accepted; the tests check the rule and that you used exactly the given values.

Try to do it in place with O(1) extra space.

examples.why: Index 2 held the odd 3 and index 3 held the even 8, so they swap. [8, 3, 4, 1] would also be accepted.
The only valid order puts the even 6 at index 0.
Both odds start out on the left. Sorting even values first, [2, 4, 7, 9], is not enough: the slots have to alternate.

constraints: Exactly half of the values are even
hints: The easy way uses a second array: drop evens into slots 0, 2, 4… and odds into 1, 3, 5… Can you avoid the extra array?
Misplaced values come in pairs: every odd value on an even slot is matched by some even value on an odd slot, because the counts are equal.
Walk one pointer over even slots and one over odd slots. When the even-slot pointer finds an odd value, advance the odd-slot pointer to the next even value, swap them, and continue.

explain.intuition:
Because there are exactly as many evens as even slots, the misplaced values balance out: if some even slot holds an odd value, then some odd slot must hold an even value. Swapping that pair fixes both at once.

So keep two pointers: i visits even slots and j visits odd slots, both only moving forward. Whenever nums[i] is odd, move j forward by 2 until nums[j] is even, then swap. Neither pointer ever goes back, so the whole thing is O(n) with no extra array, like partitioning in quicksort but with two interleaved lanes.
steps: Copy the input (or work in place) and set j = 1.
For i = 0, 2, 4, …: if nums[i] is even, it is already fine.
Otherwise, while nums[j] is odd, add 2 to j. Then swap nums[i] and nums[j].
pitfalls: Sorting evens before odds. That groups them, it does not alternate them.
Resetting j to 1 for every i. Odd slots before j are already correct, so restarting makes it O(n²).
Moving j by 1 instead of 2 and swapping an even value into an even slot with another even value.

solutions.title: Fill two lanes from a copy
solutions.idea: Write each even value into the next free even slot and each odd value into the next free odd slot.

solutions.title: Swap misplaced pairs with two pointers
solutions.idea: One pointer walks even slots, one walks odd slots. Each odd value on an even slot is swapped with the next even value on an odd slot.

followups: The counts are no longer equal. Place as many values as possible on matching slots and the rest at the end.
Keep the relative order of the evens and of the odds. Can you still do it in O(1) extra space?
